item.title: Chicago Bears say 'sole focus' is building new stadium in Indiana and reveal how that will affect their name
item.description: The Chicago Bears announced their "sole focus" is now on planning a world-class stadium and mixed-use development project in Hammond, Indiana.
item.content:encoded:
The Chicago Bears on Thursday announced that their new stadium planning and expectations, which the team had been balancing between options in Arlington Heights, Illinois and Hammond Indiana, will now have a "sole focus" on the site in the state next door.

The club is definitely leaving Chicago, which it has called home since 1921.

And it is almost definitely leaving Illinois, too.

CHICAGO BEARS TAKE MAJOR STEP TOWARD LEAVING CITY AFTER MORE THAN A CENTURY AS FRANCHISE MAKES INDIANA PLANS

"...Even though we've had occasional meetings with the state of Illinois, our sole focus at this point in time is working on a world-class stadium and mixed use development in Hammond, Indiana," Bears CEO Kevin Warren told reporters on Thursday.

So, the Indiana Bears?

The Hammond Bears?

Nope.

"We will be the Chicago Bears, whether we're in Arlington or whether we're in Hammond," Bears Chairman George McCaskey said. "And as Kevin said, our focus on Hammond, that's where we're advancing our efforts, and that's where the bulk of our time, attention, and resources are being devoted."

McCaskey said he understands there is anxiety from Bears fans that the club is likely leaving the state.

"We understand that that's out there," he said. "And it needs to be dealt with. We are doing surveying, research, data collection, to address those issues. And as I said months ago, this is going to require an adjustment.

"But it required an adjustment when we went from Wrigley [Field] to Soldier [Field]. It required an adjustment when we went from, Soldier to Champaign temporarily. And it required an adjustment when we came back to the quote unquote new Soldier Field.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"That's how it works over the course of 100-years-plus of franchise stewardship."

For months there has been hope among some fans and others in Illinois that some sort of Hail Mary proposal or scheme could somehow keep the Bears from bolting. That would require work with the mostly Democrat politicians in Illinois from Gov. J.B. Pritzker to legislators and McCaskey made it clear those discussions with Illinois politicians haven't been fruitful.

"Minimal," McCaskey said describing the communication. "We were waiting to see whether there would be some substantive action taken. We thought we had presented a pretty compelling case that a stadium in Arlington would be beneficial not only for the village of Arlington Heights, but for the community, and for the entire state.

"Really a tremendous driver of economic activity, job creation, tax revenue, sales revenue, and ultimately that argument was unsuccessful."

CHICAGO POLITICIANS ARE DOING WINDY CITY POLITICIAN THINGS TO TRY TO KEEP THE BEARS IN TOWN

The mostly Republican politicians in Indiana, meanwhile, have offered a stark contrast.

"The representatives from the state of Indiana, all the way from the governor's office to representatives in Northwest Indiana, have been phenomenal partners," Warren said. "They've been stellar to work with, very professional, diligent, with a can-do attitude."

item.title: Prichard Colon, boxer left in vegetative state after illegal punches in 2015 bout, dead at 33
item.description: Prichard Colon, who suffered a subdural hematoma after illegal punches in his 2015 bout against Terrel Williams, has died at 33 after years in care.
item.content:encoded:
Prichard Colon, the former boxer who fell into a coma in 2015 following a controversial match, has died. He was 33.

The news was shared by Colon’s father, Richard, on Thursday, announcing the heartbreaking news about his son.

"Good morning, my people. I regret to inform you of the passing of my son Prichard from this earthly world," he wrote on Facebook, translated from Spanish. "Now he is in a better world.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"I did everything possible to fulfill his wish, his dream of bringing him on vacation on Puerto Rico as much as he desired, but couldn’t. Thank you for so many years of love and prayers. As much as you can, please keep us in your prayers."

Colon was one of boxing’s rising stars in 2015, owning a 16-0 record with 13 knockouts to his name ahead of his fight to Terrel Williams.

BOXER PRICHARD COLÓN TAKEN OFF SEDATIVES, FAMILY PRAYS HE WAKES FROM COMA

But during that bout, Colon was repeatedly hit in the back of the head by illegal punches. He tried telling the referee about it, but the fight continued on.

While Williams wasn’t docked for the illegal hits, Colon was hit with a two-point penalty for a low blow on his opponent.

In the end, Colon hit the canvas in the ninth round, and his team removed his gloves while he was down thinking the fight was over. It, in fact, wasn’t and Colon was disqualified.

However, a more serious situation occurred when he needed help getting to the locker room. He vomited and collapsed, immediately leading to his team getting him to the hospital.

Colon was diagnosed with a subdural hematoma, and he underwent an emergency procedure to reduce brain swelling.

As a result, Colon fell into a coma that lasted 221 days. Upon waking up, he was in a vegetative state, unable to speak without using a computer.

Colon needed to be cared for by his family up until his death.

Colon finished his boxing career as an honorary WBC World Champion and a gold medal winner at the 2010 Pan American Youth Championship in the 64 kilogram weight class.

item.title: 'Deadpool' star Rob Delaney reveals how losing 2-year-old son changed his approach to fame
item.description: Rob Delaney reveals how losing his son Henry to a brain tumor at age two reshaped his entire approach to Hollywood and his career priorities.
item.content:encoded:
The death of Rob Delaney's son, Henry, fundamentally changed the way he approaches Hollywood, prompting the "Deadpool" star to limit his workload and spend as much time as possible at home with his children.

Delaney lost his two-and-a-half-year-old son in 2018 after battling a brain tumor. Henry had been diagnosed with cancer shortly after his 1st birthday.

"I had a son, his name was Henry, and he died, and he's dead," he said during an appearance on Ted Danson's podcast, "Where Everybody Knows Your Name." "You know, does he live on inside of me and in the smile of my wife and in the gaze of my other boys who are alive and vibrant? Yes, he does. But he died, and I don't like to sugarcoat that, you know. And that affected how I work now."

RYAN GOSLING'S FAMILY-FIRST PHILOSOPHY RESHAPED HIS HOLLYWOOD CAREER: EXPERTS

Rather than building a production empire or juggling numerous projects like some peers, he chose to prioritize being physically present with his family.

"...they've got their fingers in other pies," he said. "I don't do that. I just do one, maybe two things at a time to the best of my abilities, and then I just spend the rest of the time at home, you know, smelling my kids and having as many of them sit on me at one time as possible, you know."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

For Delaney, that shift in priorities is inseparable from the grief he continues to carry.

"That's a big part of me is metabolizing that the pain of the loss of Henry and then trying to be smart enough to let that inform how I do my career, because I think it would be a real shame if that happened and I didn't change how I work, you know," he explained. "That would be folly."

Delaney spent years working in stand-up before gaining a major following on Twitter, where his offbeat comedy helped turn him into one of the platform’s earliest breakout comedians. In 2012, he was named "Funniest Person on Twitter" at Comedy Central’s Comedy Awards.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

His biggest career breakthrough came with "Catastrophe," the acclaimed comedy series he co-created, co-wrote and starred in alongside Sharon Horgan from 2015 to 2019.

Some of Delaney's biggest roles include "Deadpool 2", "Mission: Impossible – Dead Reckoning Part One," "Deadpool & Wolverine" and "Dying for Sex."

item.title: Fury erupts as 37-year illegal alien demands citizenship in viral Spanish rant alongside Dem leaders
item.description: A viral video clip shows an illegal alien demanding amnesty in Spanish alongside Democratic Party leaders, sparking fierce backlash over immigration laws.
item.content:encoded:
Furious users took to social media to blast an illegal alien who has been present in the United States for 37 years after she demanded amnesty in a Spanish rant alongside top Democratic Party leaders.

"I ask that you be champions of a change in the immigration laws," said Margarita Cielo Balbuena, flanked by House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and Rep. Rob Menendez, D-N.J., through an interpreter earlier this week.

"We need a path to citizenship for those of us that have been present for at least seven years in this country," she continued. "We need a stop to these raids that immigration is using to terrorize Dover [New Jersey]."

ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT TOP DEM FOUGHT TO FREE TURNS UP ON VOTER ROLLS: 'MOCKERY OF OUR IMMIGRATION LAWS'

A clip of the video went viral online Wednesday.

"It is not just that someone like me, who has been in this country since 1989, who pays taxes, who is a homeowner, who is a business owner who gives work to others, someone who has children and grandchildren who are born in this country — that I have to suffer the psychological and physical abuse and that I also have to suffer the humiliation that is the violent arrest and detention in a detention center," said Cielo Balbuena.

The foreign-born woman was detained in ICE's Elizabeth Detention Center for two months, and claimed that she was treated inhumanely, according to the New Jersey Globe.

But online opponents of illegal immigration were not sympathetic to Cielo Balbuena's call.

ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT WHO MURDERED MICHIGAN WOMAN SUES TRUMP, DEMANDS $75M, PUBLIC APOLOGY, US CITIZENSHIP

Among her most prominent and harshest critics was former U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) commander-at-large Gregory Bovino.

"You have lived in the United States since 1989. That is 37 years. You still need a translator," he listed.

"At a Democratic event you stood up and demanded a path to citizenship for anyone who has been here just 7 years," Bovino continued. "Notice the arrogance. Notice the entitlement."

He went on to claim that Democrats' open borders policies allowed so many foreigners into the country so quickly that "assimilation is no longer required."

"There can be no amnesty and there can be no exceptions. All illegals must go," the John Birch Society said on X in response to the video.

DEMOCRAT COMPARES ICE TO 'DOMESTIC TERRORISTS' AS 111 HOUSE DEMS DEMAND TEXAS DETENTION CENTER CLOSE

"No English. No citizenship," said popular online personality Brigitte Gabriel.

"No. Someone who wanted to be a citizen would care enough to learn the language. In any country," said another post that garnered over 1,000 likes.

"Immediate deportation," said actor Matthew Marsden. "A just country that cares about its citizens should defend it. That includes getting rid of people like this."

Rep. Jeffries spoke at the event, and demanded the closure of Delaney Hall, another ICE detention facility in New Jersey that was subject to intense protests and sometimes violent riots for months earlier this year.

GEORGIA ICE SWEEP NABS OVER 700 CRIMINAL ILLEGAL ALIENS, INCLUDING SEX OFFENDERS, CHILD ABUSERS

"Delaney Hall needs to be shut down," Jeffries said. "That will remain a high priority for us until it takes place."

"The behavior that ICE is engaging in is inconsistent with our values and what America should represent."

The White House fired back in a statement to Fox News Digital, saying: "These types of smears by sanctuary politicians are contributing to our ICE law enforcement officers facing a more than 1,300% increase in assaults against them and an 8,000% increase in death threats."

"Our ICE officers are heroes who put their lives on the line to arrest murderers, rapists, pedophiles, gang members, and terrorists from American communities. Democrats must stop demonizing our officers for simply enforcing our nation’s laws," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said.

item.title: Resurfaced WNBA post shows league celebrating males who stole wins from female athletes
item.description: A resurfaced 2021 WNBA post celebrated trans athletes Andraya Yearwood and Terry Miller while the league now says it needs months to define eligibility.
item.content:encoded:
The WNBA apparently needs "weeks and months" to figure out whether biological males should be eligible to play in a professional basketball league for women.

Five years ago, the league didn't seem nearly as confused.

CLUELESS WNBA ATTACKS 'BAD-FAITH' FANS WHO DON'T WANT BIOLOGICAL MEN RUINING WOMEN'S SPORTS

A resurfaced June 2021 post from the WNBA’s official X (formerly Twitter) account, which was also shared on Facebook, celebrated Andraya Yearwood and Terry Miller, two males who competed in girls' high school track in Connecticut and were at the center of a major legal fight after beating female athletes in championship events.

"Our first #WCW of #WNBAPride goes out to Andraya Yearwood and Terry Miller," the WNBA wrote.

Yes, the Women's National Basketball Association used its first "Woman Crush Wednesday" of Pride Month to celebrate two males.

"We see you. We support you and all of the other trans athletes just trying to compete in the sports they love," the league added.

The post remains live on X and the same message is still posted on the WNBA's official Facebook account.

The WNBA knew who it was celebrating. Yearwood and Miller had already become nationally known for winning girls’ track titles and finishing ahead of female athletes in Connecticut.

Those girls had names, too.

Selina Soule. Chelsea Mitchell. Alanna Smith. Ashley Nicoletti.

Funny, the WNBA's post didn't mention them.

Yearwood began competing in girls' track in 2017 under Connecticut Interscholastic Athletic Conference rules and won the Class M state championship in both the 100- and 200-meter events that year. A federal district court ruling recounting the plaintiffs' allegations says Yearwood's advancement to the State Open displaced Chelsea Mitchell, a female, from qualifying.

Miller began competing in girls' track the following year. At the 2018 Outdoor State Open, Miller and Yearwood finished first and second in the girls' 100 meters. The court noted that Mitchell would have finished second statewide without their participation. Miller also won the 200 meters.

Then came 2019.

At the State Indoor Open, Miller and Yearwood finished first and second in both the preliminary and final 55-meter races. According to the court record, Mitchell would have won the final without them and Soule would have advanced to the next stage of competition. Later that spring, Miller won another state championship over Mitchell, while Miller also won the State Open 200-meter final ahead of Smith.

Nicoletti was affected, too. The plaintiffs sought revisions to 2019 race results that included events where Miller and Yearwood finished ahead of Nicoletti, along with numerous races where one or both finished ahead of Soule, Mitchell and Smith.

By the time the WNBA posted its support in 2021, there was no mystery about the controversy surrounding Yearwood and Miller. The post itself points to one reason why: the league credited Athlete Ally, an organization that had already honored both athletes at its 2019 Action Awards.

Athlete Ally’s announcement specifically noted that Yearwood had won the 100- and 200-meter dashes and that Miller had won the State Open 200-meter title for the second consecutive year. It also referenced the legal effort challenging their participation in girls’ track.

And guess who Athlete Ally listed among the supporters of those 2019 awards?

The NBA and WNBA.

WNBPA ISSUES STATEMENT EMBRACING DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION AMID TRANS ATHLETE DEBATE IN WOMEN'S SPORTS

Two years later, the WNBA officially partnered with Athlete Ally for Pride Month. A league press release said one of the WNBA/WNBPA Social Justice Council's priorities was LGBTQ advocacy "with a focus on trans rights," and the league announced that Athlete Ally would conduct educational sessions for WNBA teams on "trans inclusivity."

The WNBA was clearly on board with male participation in girls' and women’s sports.

Meanwhile, the girls who actually raced Yearwood and Miller were the ones dealing with the consequences.

Alliance Defending Freedom, which represents Soule, Mitchell, Smith and Nicoletti in their lawsuit against Connecticut officials, has published extensive accounts of what those girls say they lost while competing against males.

Mitchell was one of the best female sprinters in Connecticut. In 2019, she said she was "ranked the fastest biological female in the state of Connecticut," yet she had to repeatedly watch championship honors go to male competitors.

"When I have to compete against a transgender athlete, I just feel completely defeated before I even run the race," Mitchell said.

Think about that for a second.

Mitchell was fast enough to win state championships. In several championship races, she was the fastest female on the track, yet the title still went to a male competitor.

Soule described realizing the problem almost immediately when she first raced against a male athlete as a freshman.

"I knew right then and there that some girls will be missing out on great opportunities to succeed, and that women could be completely eradicated from their own sports," she said.

In the 2019 indoor State Open, Miller and Yearwood took the top two spots while Soule missed advancing.

The consequences went beyond titles and qualifying spots. For Ashley Nicoletti, simply lining up against a male competitor changed how she viewed the race before it even started.

"I felt nervous even at the thought of such an unfair race," Nicoletti told ADF. "I knew I had a chance against other girls, but not against a male athlete."

Those were the girls losing titles and opportunities while the WNBA was backing athletes like Yearwood and Miller.

Mitchell lost championship recognition; Soule lost an opportunity to advance; and, Nicoletti described knowing before the race even started that she couldn't fairly compete.

Yet the WNBA's message to Yearwood and Miller was: "We see you. We support you."

Where was that support for the girls who actually lost to them?

And then there's Alanna Smith.

Miller finished ahead of Smith in championship competition, including winning the 200-meter final at the 2019 State Open. ADF recounts a conversation between Smith and her mother on the way to a meet in New York City. Her mother asked what her strategy was going to be that day.

Smith's response?

"Mom, it really doesn't matter, because I'm running against the boys today."

Fast-forward five years, and that certainty is gone. Male participation in women’s sports is now apparently a question requiring extended consultation.

On paper, the new collective bargaining agreement appears to provide a clear answer: "Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA."

Except the 409-page agreement doesn’t define "woman," and the league has repeatedly declined to tell OutKick/Fox News Digital whether a biological male who identifies as a woman would satisfy that requirement.

The issue escalated after former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White announced that they planned to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft, directly challenging the league's undefined eligibility language.

The WNBA convened a task force this week amid pressure to answer the question. It emerged without a definition and said it would spend the coming "weeks and months" continuing discussions with league stakeholders.

But here's the part that really tells the story.

A source familiar with the league and with Wednesday's meeting told Fox News that the meeting "focused significantly on the hate and vitriol being directed at WNBA players online."

So, amid mounting questions about who is eligible to compete in a women’s league, the WNBA spent a significant portion of its meeting discussing "hate and vitriol" directed at players online.

That’s the priority?

RILEY GAINES SAYS WNBA IS 'HELLBENT' ON BEING AN ACTIVIST ORGANIZATION OVER A BASKETBALL LEAGUE

The WNBA’s sudden concern about the tone of the conversation is pretty rich. Criticism of the league’s eligibility policy isn’t the same thing as hatred, and asking whether males should be eligible to compete against women isn’t "demeaning" anyone.

Four female athletes told the world that they were losing championships, advancement opportunities and recognition because they were being forced to compete against males. The WNBA didn't issue a statement expressing concern for their well-being. It didn't announce that it needed to engage stakeholders to make sure female athletes were being treated fairly.

It celebrated the males who beat them.

WNBA star Sophie Cunningham put the issue in plain terms, saying girls shouldn’t have to "go against biological men."

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

But the league still hasn’t said whether a biological male could be eligible to play in the WNBA.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

In 2021, while males Andraya Yearwood and Terry Miller were taking titles and opportunities from girls, the WNBA publicly backed them.

"We see you. We support you."

The girls they beat got a very different message.

item.title: Social media has a field day with Texas A&M player for looking like a 36-year-old construction worker
item.description: Texas A&M defensive end Anto Saka thanked strength coach Tommy Moffitt for his offseason gains, but his mature looks had social media in disbelief.
item.content:encoded:
Offseason transformations are one of the coolest parts about college football.

It's simply amazing to see what six to eight months in a Division I strength and conditioning program can do for a group of young men, especially considering that, for the majority of them, this is the first time they've seriously thrown some weight around in their lives.

High school gym does not prepare you for 5 a.m. lifts with an SEC strength coach, and it shows with how different these kids look between their freshman and sophomore years.

OKLAHOMA SOONERS QUARTERBACK JOHN MATEER LOOKS ABSOLUTELY JACKED JUST IN TIME FOR FALL CAMP

One player who has seen plenty of gains since entering a college weight room is Texas A&M defensive end Anto Saka, and he expressed his gratitude to Aggies strength coach Tommy Moffitt during an interview on Wednesday.

I'm not sure what Moffitt and the Aggies are putting in their post-workout protein shakes, though, because Saka's mature looks caught the eye of the entire internet earlier this week.

You're trying to tell me that's a college kid? Because he looks like a 36-year-old construction worker with two kids and a mortgage.

I know redshirt rules have gotten a little out of hand in college sports recently, but there's no way this 30-something union worker has any eligibility left to play football.

I looked it up, and apparently Saka is a 22-year-old college senior.

Sure, Jan.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL COACHES ON HOT SEAT: BILL BELICHICK, MIKE NORVELL AND OTHERS FACING MAKE-OR-BREAK 2026

He was allegedly born in 2002, which means Saka wasn't even alive when the Twin Towers fell, yet he looks old enough to have worked there.

I'm 33 years old, and if I ever interviewed this kid, I'm pretty sure I'd call him "sir."

Social media had an absolute field day with Saka, dropping memes left and right poking fun at the world's oldest looking guy who can't legally rent a car yet.

If Hollywood were to cast this young man to portray a college student in a movie, we would all collectively complain about how they never get actors to play characters their age.

He's like a real-life Luke Perry in "90210."

Anyway, congrats on the big gains in the weight room, Anto!

Just remember to stretch for ten minutes before every lift. A guy your age could really mess his back up throwing weight around like that.

item.title: Pro wrestling icon Matt Hardy puts first tag team ladder match in historical perspective
item.description: Matt Hardy reveals the 1999 tag team ladder match with Edge and Christian that he says launched the TLC concept and changed pro wrestling forever.
item.content:encoded:
Whichever version of Matt Hardy a pro wrestling fan may have enjoyed over the course of his more than 35 years in the sport, his innovative mind and versatile in-ring abilities may be what he will get remembered for the most when he finally decides to hang up his boots.

Hardy has been a scene-stealer in almost every company he’s worked for whether it was WWE, All Elite Wrestling (AEW), Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA), Ring of Honor or elsewhere.

The 51-year-old multi-time champion has nearly done everything in the business. 

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON FOX NEWS DIGITAL

Fox News Digital asked Hardy in a recent interview which moment of his career he thought doesn’t get talked about enough. Hardy pointed to the first-ever tag team ladder match he and his brother, Jeff, had with Edge and Christian at No Mercy 1999.

He said the match helped pave the way for the historic tables, ladders and chairs match that took place at SummerSlam 2000 and innovated the way inanimate objects are used in the wrestling ring.

"It’s crazy because my brother and I, we've been blessed to have so many great moments over our, Oct. 15 we'll be going into our 35th year of doing this as pro wrestlers, which is crazy," Hardy said. 

"A moment still that I don't think gets talked about quite enough – it got praised, especially when it happened, but just looking back at how monumental it was in changing the game, was the first ever tag team ladder match I think.

BZZR 'CUTTING OUT THE NOISE' FROM SPORTS SOCIAL MEDIA SPACE GREAT FOR CREATORS, SPORTSCASTER JON ALBA SAYS

"I still think it was so instrumental in leading the way for change in the way of telling stories with inanimate objects in WWE because that ultimately led to us doing the first-ever tag team tables match with the Dudleys, which is an idea I presented to Vince (McMahon). He wanted to do something with the Dudleys that paralleled what we did with Edge and Christian. 

"And then that led to us using all of these items in WrestleMania 2000 and then ultimately at SummerSlam 2000, we did the first ever TLC, tables, ladders and chairs match and that has become a staple in pro wrestling and even in other companies."

Hardy pointed to other companies using similar matches, including AEW, TNA’s Full Metal Mayhem and Ring of Honor’s Ladder Wars.

"But that tag team ladder match that we did with Edge and Christian is something that was like absolutely the beginning and origin point of the TLC concept and that became a staple in pro wrestling and myself and Jeff and Edge and Christian without us having that match that doesn't become a thing.

So that is a moment I think historically, years down the road, decades down the road, people will look back at that and they go, ‘Wow, that was the moment where all of this insanity started.’ And there was a different way of telling stories with these inanimate objects doing a different version of storytelling, doing a different version of match that can be exciting and athletic guys can really benefit from it."

Now, as his career gets set to turn 35, Hardy and his brother are the current TNA world tag team champions. He also hosts a podcast with Jon Alba, sharing stories and memories from his career.

"The Extreme Life of Matt Hardy" drops a new episode each Friday on his YouTube page.

item.title: DiJonai Carrington reportedly had fan escorted from his seat over an 'unfounded' accusation
item.description: DiJonai Carrington slapped two players, picked up a technical foul and got a fan ejected over a complaint that was later found unfounded.
item.content:encoded:

It's unclear what Carrington accused the fan of saying. The USA Network broadcast captured part of the incident during the game.

"So, there is a stoppage right now as Chicago’s team security has stepped out along with arena security representatives," the broadcast informed viewers.

"Carrington went over to one of the officials, as you see Sarah Williams there, to say something."

Watch below:

She continues to conduct herself like a professional victim. This was the case even before she clotheslined Sophie Cunningham, posted "white privilege" on social media from the locker room and then claimed her accusation of racism wasn't about the hard foul she committed.

Even if/when Carrington reveals what she told officials the fan allegedly shouted at her, we cannot take her word for it. These are the consequences of her behavior. People stop believing you.

Apparently, that includes officials, who let the fan return to his seat after determining Carrington's complaint was "unfounded."

Likewise, we can no longer take Angel Reese seriously when she cries racism, given the similarly unfounded nature of her many accusations against fans.

For those who can't figure out why Sophie Cunningham and Caitlin Clark are so much more popular than other WNBA players, this is part of the reason why. Cunningham and Clark conduct themselves like professionals. They are likeable.

Conversely, players like Carrington act like entitled, dishonest wannabe victims.

item.title: The scammer at your doctor's office may already know who you are
item.description: QR code scams at doctor's offices use data brokers and people search websites to craft personalized phishing attacks targeting your Medicare number.
item.content:encoded:
You arrive at your doctor’s office and see a sign asking you to scan a QR code to check in. Later, you receive a text about a prescription. A Medicare notice with your name and address arrives in the mail. Before you leave, another QR code asks you to pay for parking. 

All of it looks routine. That’s exactly what can make these scams so dangerous. Criminals aren’t limited to sending obvious phishing messages to random people. Personal information available through data brokers and people search websites can help scammers create medical, Medicare and payment scams that look like they were meant specifically for you.

Then a QR code gives them an easy way to send you to a convincing fake website asking for your Medicare number, patient portal login, credit card information or other sensitive data. Here’s what to watch for during your next trip to the doctor’s office and one important step that can make you harder for scammers to target in the first place.

QR codes have become a normal part of healthcare. Doctors’ offices use them for check-in forms. Pharmacies use them for pickup information. Medicare Advantage and Part D plans may include them in enrollment materials and other communications. Hospitals and medical buildings increasingly use QR codes for parking payments. That familiarity works in a scammer’s favor. When you’re standing inside your doctor’s office holding paperwork that looks official or looking at a sign next to a parking machine, you naturally expect the information to be legitimate. Scammers know that.

A QR code also hides something that a normal web link does not: where it is actually taking you. You can usually glance at a link in an email before clicking it. With a QR code, you see a square filled with black and white patterns. You don’t know where it leads until your phone reads it. That makes the location of the QR code itself part of the deception.

The mechanics of the scam are surprisingly simple.

A criminal can:

Scan the code, and you may land on a website designed to resemble your insurer, pharmacy, doctor’s portal or payment processor.

The site may ask for your:

QR code phishing is sometimes called "quishing." The challenge is that many people have become so accustomed to QR codes that scanning one no longer feels like clicking a link.

This is where these scams can become much more convincing. A criminal contacting you may already have access to details such as your:

Some of that information can appear on data broker and people search websites. Think about the difference between receiving a generic message that says: "Your health coverage has changed" and receiving a notice addressed to you by name, sent to your correct home address and written to resemble something connected to Medicare or your health coverage. The second message feels far more believable. That’s why protecting yourself isn’t only about spotting a fake QR code. It's also about reducing the amount of personal information strangers can easily find about you online.

FAKE VA SHOE OFFER TARGETS VETERANS

These examples show how fraudulent QR codes can blend into places where people already expect to see them.

One Medicare beneficiary described receiving a letter that appeared to come from a major insurer and directed the recipient to scan a QR code to read an Annual Notice of Change. The letter reportedly closely resembled legitimate plan correspondence, but the QR code pointed to a shortened, lookalike web address instead of the insurer’s actual domain. This particular example is a reported account rather than a confirmed investigated incident, but it follows a familiar scam pattern: make an official-looking Medicare communication feel urgent and legitimate, then direct the victim somewhere controlled by the scammer.

At Totnes Community Hospital in the U.K., a fraudulent QR code sticker was discovered on a parking payment machine. One visitor who scanned the code to pay reportedly had £146.79 taken from her account. The scammers then attempted to take another £849 before her bank’s fraud team intervened. The hospital trust confirmed the fraudulent code and began monitoring payment machines at other locations.

Law enforcement in Redondo Beach and San Clemente, California, has documented scammers placing counterfeit QR code stickers next to legitimate parking payment instructions. A medical office or hospital parking structure can be an especially convincing place for this trick because people already expect to scan something to pay.

Older Americans frequently interact with healthcare systems, pharmacies, insurance providers and Medicare.

That means a message about a doctor's appointment, prescription pickup, Medicare coverage, insurance changes, medical paperwork or hospital parking may not seem unusual. Add accurate personal information to the message, and the scam can become even harder to recognize. That’s the real danger. The QR code might be the thing you scan, but the personal details surrounding it are what can make you trust it.

A few quick checks can help you determine whether a QR code deserves your trust.

Most modern phones display the destination before opening a QR code link. Look carefully at the web address. If the domain is unfamiliar, shortened, misspelled or slightly different from the organization’s normal website, don't continue.

If a receptionist, sign or piece of paperwork tells you to scan a QR code, there's nothing wrong with asking, "Is this your official QR code?" That simple question can protect you if someone has placed a fraudulent sticker over a legitimate code.

Before scanning a QR code on a sign, parking meter or payment machine, look closely. Be suspicious if the code:

An official-looking envelope does not guarantee that what’s inside is legitimate. If a Medicare or insurance notice tells you to scan a QR code, consider going directly to the organization’s known website instead. You can also call the phone number printed on your insurance card rather than relying on contact information supplied in an unexpected mailing.

FCC ROBOCALL CRACKDOWN COULD CHANGE PHONE PRIVACY

Whenever possible, use your healthcare provider’s official app or type its known website address directly into your browser. The same rule applies to Medicare, pharmacies and insurers. Don’t trust a QR code simply because it appears in a place you trust.

Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) for accounts that support it, especially:

Two-factor authentication adds another barrier even if a scammer manages to obtain your password.

Install operating system, browser and security updates when they become available. Updates can help protect against dangerous websites, malicious downloads and other threats you might encounter after scanning a fraudulent code.

If you see a QR code at a doctor’s office, hospital, pharmacy or parking facility that appears suspicious, tell an employee. Removing one fraudulent sticker could prevent many other people from scanning it. You can also report suspected fraud to the Federal Trade Commission at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

Spotting a fraudulent QR code can protect you from one scam. Reducing the personal information available about you can make it harder for scammers to build convincing attacks in the first place. Data brokers and people search websites can expose information such as your name, address, phone number, age range and household details. Those pieces of information may seem harmless on their own. Put together, they can give a criminal enough background information to make a Medicare notice, medical message or other scam feel surprisingly personal.

You can contact data brokers and people search sites yourself and request that your information be removed. The challenge is that your information may appear across many different sites and can sometimes return after it has been removed.

A personal data removal service can help automate that process by sending removal requests to data brokers on your behalf and continuing to check whether your information reappears. No service can guarantee that every piece of personal information will disappear from the internet, but reducing what is easily available can give scammers fewer details to work with when trying to create a convincing, personalized attack.

Whether you handle removals yourself or use a service, periodically search for your name, phone number and address online to see what strangers can find. The less information that is readily available about you, the harder it can be for a scammer to make a fake medical message, Medicare notice or payment request look legitimate.

The most convincing scams don’t always feel random. They may include your name, address or other accurate personal details that make a fake medical notice, Medicare communication or payment request feel legitimate. A QR code at your doctor’s office, in a healthcare mailing or on a hospital parking machine can simply be the final step that sends you to a fraudulent website. 

Before scanning, check the destination, look for signs of tampering and confirm unfamiliar codes with staff. Whenever possible, go directly to the organization’s official website or app. Just as importantly, find out how much personal information about you is publicly available online. The less information scammers can easily find about you, the harder it becomes for them to create a scam that feels like it was made specifically for you.

item.title: Stephen A Smith roasts Stephanie White after DiJonai Carrington foul response: 'How are you the head coach?'
item.description: Stephen A. Smith eviscerated Indiana Fever head coach Stephanie White, questioning her response to DiJonai Carrington's foul on Sophie Cunningham.
item.content:encoded:
Stephen A. Smith had some strong words to share about Indiana Fever head coach Stephanie White, even questioning how she can be in her position.

The ESPN personality went on a rant calling out White for how she handled the aftermath of DiJonai Carrington’s Flagrant 2 foul on her Fever star, Sophie Cunningham, this past weekend. Carrington smacked Cunningham across the face, leading to the flagrant foul and ejection from the game.

During White’s post-game news conference, she actually praised Carrington’s aggressive play before claiming she didn’t see the whole play in the moment and couldn’t comment any further on it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

White has since issued a pre-rehearsed, fiery defense of herself before Tuesday’s win against the New York Liberty.

"You know, this isn't necessarily for those people that are in this room. This is more for an online community that's trying to create narratives that simply don't exist," White said to reporters. "Trying to create a fabrication or distortion of who I am, of what I'm about. Our players' success, our players' health and wellness, our players' safety is always a top priority for me. One of the things I pride myself on is my relationships with players."

Smith wasn’t buying it, and neither were Fever fans as boos rained down during the team’s home game on Tuesday.

"There are folks in Indiana at a home game booing you!" Smith said passionately on his show. "You ain’t the road team. You’re the home team … and they’re booing you!"

DIJONAI CARRINGTON RESPONDS TO 'WHITE PRIVILEGE' POST, BUT LEAVES MEANING OF IT STILL UNCLEAR

Smith also didn’t understand how White couldn’t see the whole play in question, one that continues to be talked about especially as Carrington remains mysterious as to why she posted "WHITE PRIVILEGE @indianafever" on Threads immediately following her ejection.

"How are you the head coach…and you didn’t see the play? It’s your job to…watch the game. How did you not see the play?" Smith said.

White simply said after Saturday’s game that she didn’t think "DiJonai intentionally came out to get [Cunningham] to get her across the neck like she did, but it did happen and I thought it was the right call." But then she went on to defend Carrington’s play.

"One of the things about [Carrington] is that she’s gonna play her butt off, man," White, who used to coach Carrington with the Connecticut Sun, said. "She’s gonna compete. Nobody’s gonna go walking in for a layup. And so I don’t oppose the hard foul, but I also don’t think that she intentionally went for the neck."

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

Carrington’s foul wasn’t just hard, but a full clothesline of Cunningham, who understandably got right up to confront the Chicago Sky guard. Cunningham gave a light shove to Carrington as teammates were trying to separate her before things got even uglier.

"For those who have anything to say about the play in the last game, I didn’t see the play in real time," White said during her defense on Tuesday. "I went straight to a press conference. I thought the play got called right. Thankfully, Sophie’s OK. Was it egregious? Absolutely. When you have a chance to watch that over and over and over on replay, you can see that. I didn’t have that in real time. I take personally any suggestions that I don’t 100% always have my players’ back. I ride with them 10 toes down all the time. All the time. They know that."

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

While White heard boos from the stands, the Fever got the job done against their rival Liberty squad, 108-92. But Clark admitted the jeers from the crowd made her "a little sick," while Cunningham stated her knowledge that "Coach loves" this team.

The Fever will return home on Friday night to face Paige Bueckers and the Dallas Wings at 7:30 p.m. ET.

item.title: Rumer Willis takes a 'leap of faith' and moves across country to Nashville
item.description: Rumer Willis shared a video of her cross-country move to Nashville shortly after a California judge granted her temporary primary custody of her daughter.
item.content:encoded:
Rumer Willis is thrilled to be starting a new chapter in Nashville.

On Wednesday, Willis took to Instagram and shared a video of her packing up her life and taking a "leap of faith" for her cross-country move.

"Moving your whole life across the country is a leap of faith," the daughter of Bruce Willis and Demi Moore began, crediting Roadway Movers for helping streamline the "emotional" experience. "They carried two decades of my life across 2,000 miles and set it down in Nashville without a scratch."

Willis went on to share details of her move, explaining that she felt peace during the long journey.

'FIRE COUNTRY' STAR DIANE FARR REVEALS WHERE SHE NOW LIVES AFTER LEAVING LOS ANGELES BEHIND

"I got to say goodbye to my old home without worrying about what was in the truck and if it was going to make the trip in one piece. That’s worth everything during a week this emotional.

"New chapter, officially delivered."

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

In her video, Willis showed the moving company loading all of her belongings into a truck and then unloading her things at her new home in Nashville.

In early 2025, Willis announced she was leaving Los Angeles and moving to her family's home in Idaho.

Rumer's out-of-state move to Nashville came shortly after a California judge granted Willis temporary primary physical custody of her 3-year-old daughter, Louetta Isley Thomas Willis, according to E! News. Willis shares her daughter with her former partner, musician Derek Richard Thomas.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Willis and Thomas split in 2024 after about two years together.

Willis and Thomas continue to share joint legal custody, meaning they both have a role in major decisions concerning their daughter, according to People. 

The court also established a parenting schedule for Thomas that began with monitored visits and was set to transition to unmonitored overnight visits in August.

item.title: Beer, wine or liquor? Massive study reveals which was linked to lower death risk
item.description: Heavy alcohol use raised death risk by 24%, but wine at low levels was linked to lower mortality than beer or spirits in a UK Biobank study.
item.content:encoded:
Heavy drinking has been shown to raise mortality risk, but, at lower levels, what’s in your glass may also matter, a new study suggests.

In recent research of data from 340,924 participants in the UK Biobank, wine was linked to lower mortality, while beer and spirits were tied to higher death risk.

Data were collected between 2006 and 2022, with more than 13 years of average follow-up. The findings were presented at the American College of Cardiology’s Annual Scientific Session in New Orleans.

WINE EXPERT SAYS ONE COMMON HABIT COULD BE SABOTAGING EVERY SIP

In the study, participants reported their alcohol intake as never/occasional, low, moderate or high.

High consumption was defined as more than 40 grams per day for men (about three standard drinks) and more than 20 grams per day for women (about 1.4 standard drinks).

Participants with high alcohol consumption had a 24% higher risk of all-cause death, 36% higher risk of cancer death and 14% higher risk of cardiovascular death when compared to people who never or occasionally drank, according to the study findings.

With low or moderate alcohol consumption, however, the mortality risk appeared to differ according to the type of beverage.

AMERICA HITS MAJOR MARIJUANA MILESTONE AS DAILY WEED USE SURPASSES DAILY DRINKING

Spirits, beer and cider were associated with significantly higher mortality, the researchers found, while the same amount of wine intake was linked to significantly lower mortality. Moderate wine drinkers had a 21% lower risk of cardiovascular death than those who never or occasionally drank.

Conversely, those who drank low amounts of spirits, beer or cider were found to have a 9% higher risk of cardiovascular death.

"These results come from the general population, and in certain high-risk groups, such as people with chronic diseases or cardiovascular conditions, the risks could be even higher," Dr. Zhangling Chen, a professor at the Second Xiangya Hospital, Central South University in China and the study's senior author, said in a press release.

"These findings can help refine guidance, emphasizing that the health risks of alcohol depend not only on the amount of alcohol consumed but also on the type of beverage."

One potential reason for wine’s lower mortality association could be that it contains compounds such as polyphenols and antioxidants, which could have beneficial effects on blood vessels, inflammation and cardiovascular health, the researchers noted.

Jessica Steinman, a Los Angeles addiction specialist and chief clinical officer for No Matter What Recovery, said the study’s information is "helpful" but cautioned against broadly applying the findings to individuals, particularly those with a history of substance misuse.

HOME COCKTAIL MAKER SAYS GEN Z ISN'T GIVING UP ALCOHOL — THEY'RE CHANGING HOW THEY DRINK

While certain ingredients or substances might help someone with a specific issue, she expressed her concern when it comes to mental health issues and addiction.

"When we hear these stories or get this research, it becomes a ‘black and white’ larger generalization for the population, and we want to be careful with that," Steinman, who was not involved in the research, told Fox News Digital.

"Not everybody should have daily consumption of an alcoholic substance, whether it's wine, beer or certain liquors. … If there's someone who’s struggling with substances, then they really shouldn't be having it at all."

Different substances have different levels of alcohol in them, and each person metabolizes alcohol uniquely, the expert noted.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"All those kinds of things are so specific to one person or a small sect of people," she said. "So, we want to make sure anytime there's research given about something, that we're not taking it as a society and saying, ‘Let's do this,’ and not keeping it as black and white.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"Overall, more is not better, but also the higher potency of alcohol and higher percentages of alcohol is going to affect people negatively as well."

Steinman recommended consulting with a medical professional for individual guidance.

The researchers acknowledged some limitations of the study. Because it was observational in design, the study could not prove that drinking wine led to lower mortality or that other alcoholic beverages directly caused higher mortality.

Also, the participants reported their baseline alcohol intake at the start of the study, which means any changes in drinking patterns during the follow-up period were not recorded.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

There was also the chance that wine drinkers may have different dietary or other lifestyle habits that could affect their health outcomes, the researchers noted.

The UK Biobank participants also tend to be healthier than the overall population, which could limit the ability for the finding to be generalized to wider populations.

The authors called for high-quality randomized studies to confirm the differences in how drinking habits reflect mortality risk.

item.title: 'Look at me!' Justice fires back at critics who dare question his Blackness
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas reveals how Thomas Sowell's work freed him from isolation and gave him confidence to challenge Black political norms.
item.content:encoded:
Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas said his views on race and politics have led critics to question his Blackness.

"I mean, how stupid is that? Look at me," Thomas said, grabbing his arm. "You know, then they say things like, ‘Oh, black is a state of mind.’"

Thomas made the remarks during a Hoover Institution conversation with Peter Robinson that included a discussion about the role of Black Americans in politics. The conservative justice reflected on how economist Thomas Sowell, a Black conservative, helped transform his thinking on race and politics and gave him the confidence to challenge prevailing expectations about Black Americans' political views.

CLARENCE THOMAS WARNS AMERICA: LIBERTY DIES WHEN WE CHOOSE COMFORT OVER COURAGE

Thomas said that as a young man, he felt pressure to embrace certain political beliefs because he was Black and faced resistance when he began questioning them.

"You have these views, you have these instincts, but you are getting inputs from the media, from the politicians, the people who have the megaphone, the people who have the loudest voices, that tells you you’re wrong, that tells you you’re bad, that there’s something awful about you," Thomas said.

While at Yale Law School, Thomas said he bucked the push for school busing, questioning why Black families would want their children sent across town to unfamiliar schools and neighborhoods.

"I remember saying those things at Yale and people — the bottom line was, well, you shouldn’t believe that because you’re black," Thomas said.

KEY TRUMP AGENCY PUTS TOP UNIVERSITIES IN CROSSHAIRS OVER ALLEGED RACE-BASED DORM PROGRAMS

Thomas argued there was often a disconnect between positions championed by Black political leaders and the views of ordinary Black Americans, pointing to debates over school busing and racial preferences.

"If you ask the leaders, they thought one thing. If you ask the people, they thought another," Thomas said.

It was Sowell’s work, Thomas said, that helped him make sense of views he had already begun developing on his own.

A friend introduced Thomas to Sowell’s Race and Economics, which Thomas said helped free him from the isolation he had felt over his own views.

THE WELFARE STATE BROKE BLACK FAMILIES. WORK CAN HELP RESTORE THE DREAM

"It was literally like a drink of water," Thomas said. "Here’s someone who’s thought it through and it makes sense. What your instincts were have been now demonstrated in a logical, analytical way. You’re not alone." He later sought out a friendship with Sowell.

But Thomas had not always embraced Sowell’s ideas.

As a Yale student in 1972, Thomas said he "reflexively" rejected Sowell’s Black Education: Myths and Tragedies, believing that "no black man" should think that way.

Thomas said Sowell’s example helped give him the confidence to voice his own beliefs even when doing so brought criticism.

THOMAS LEAVES NOTHING LEFT UNSAID ON RACIAL GERRYMANDERING DECISION: ‘GO FURTHER’

"If they can prove you wrong, fine," Thomas said. "But if they call you names or say you’re not black, I mean, how stupid is that? Look at me."

He tied those attacks to what he described as a broader pressure on Black Americans to conform to certain views.

"There’s this overriding public view that you’re not supposed to think this way, therefore you’re not black, therefore you’re discredited," Thomas said. "Nothing you say matters."

But for Thomas, the biggest lesson he took from Sowell was to think for himself.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"He always says what he thinks, but he never tells you to say what he wants you to think," Thomas said of Sowell. "That is yours."

"There seems to be this overwhelming pressure for us to agree with the prevailing notions which I consider almost illusory in a sense," Thomas said.

item.title: Scramble for Karoline Leavitt's replacement ensues with just weeks until Trump's spokesperson exits
item.description: Alina Habba, Stephen Miller and Scott Jennings are among the names floated to replace Karoline Leavitt as Trump's White House press secretary.
item.content:encoded:
The impending departure of President Donald Trump's top spokeswoman has speculation swirling in Washington, D.C., on who will be selected to replace Karoline Leavitt behind the press briefing room podium.

The 28-year-old White House press secretary, fresh off maternity leave, dropped a bombshell announcement on Wednesday that she will end her tenure at the end of August to spend more time with her two young children.

Now, with just two weeks left in the month, the race is on to find the next press secretary — and some predict the briefing room will see a rotating line of Trump administration officials briefing the White House press corps rather than a permanent replacement, like what happened during Leavitt's maternity leave earlier this summer.

WHITE HOUSE PLANS GUEST HOSTS FOR PRESS BRIEFINGS WHILE KAROLINE LEAVITT TAKES MATERNITY LEAVE

Secretary of State Marco Rubio held the first news conference while Leavitt was on leave, followed by Vice President JD Vance, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz.

"The next press secretary will undoubtedly be someone who has a strong existing relationship with President Trump," former Trump press secretary Sean Spicer told Fox News Digital.

"He values and understands the importance of this role in communicating his positions on policy, personnel and key issues, so I can’t imagine it not being someone currently in his orbit," Spicer added.

Spicer, known for his short tenure as White House press secretary, withdrew his name for consideration a second time around.

Alina Habba, who serves as senior advisor to the attorney general for U.S. Attorneys, was viewed as a frontrunner after Trump won re-election and is once again being floated for the role.

TRUMP SAYS KAROLINE LEAVITT WILL LEAVE WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY ROLE, BECOME OUTSIDE ADVISOR

At the time, Habba said she was "flattered" by the consideration but believed she would "be better served in other capacities."

She then served three months as counselor to the president before leaving Washington, D.C., for a controversial and turbulent position as interim attorney for the District of New Jersey. After her appointment was deemed unconstitutional, she resigned and was made senior advisor to the attorney general for United States Attorneys.

Habba, who was Trump's personal attorney and a high-profile surrogate on the 2024 campaign trail, was the early favorite on Kalshi to replace the press secretary but now ranks third behind conservative political commentator Scott Jennings and Leavitt's deputy, Anna Kelly.

Trump's principal deputy press secretary has been seen in an outward facing role. Kelly filled in for Leavitt in media hits while Leavitt was on maternity leave but has yet to take the podium for a briefing.

Jennings, a CNN contributor and former aide to President George W. Bush, was also reportedly considered for the press secretary role when Trump retook office in 2024 before he selected Leavitt. Trump has touted Jennings’ recent book and has referred to him as a "patriot" who "gets it."

TRUMP’S DC LAW-AND-ORDER BLITZ MARKS ONE YEAR WITH EYE-POPPING HAUL OF SUSPECTS

Trump's senior advisor, Stephen Miller, and his wife, Katie Miller, have been floated on social media as potential replacements.

Stephen was asked Wednesday for his thoughts on his wife, former Vice President Mike Pence's press secretary and communications director, filling Leavitt’s role. In lieu of commenting, he shot a smile in the direction of the questioner.

White House communication director Stephen Cheung is one of Trump’s most forceful defenders, wielding significant influence but largely operating behind the scenes.

Other names floated as potential contenders include Breitbart's Washington Bureau Chief Matthew Boyle and former White House deputy chief of staff Taylor Budowich.

Leavitt is Trump’s second-longest-serving press secretary with 19 months in the role. She comes in second to first-term press secretary and now Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders’ 23-month tenure.

After Huckabee's departure, Stephanie Grisham stepped into the role for nine months but was famous for not holding a single press briefing during that time. She was eventually replaced with Kayleigh McEnany, who served through the end of Trump's first term.

item.title: El-Sayed may be 'full-blown communist' despite socialist denial: top Republican
item.description: Lisa McClain calls Abdul El-Sayed a potential "full-blown communist" after his upset Michigan Senate primary win, citing his progressive platform.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan’s highest-ranking House Republican is crying foul on Abdul El-Sayed's claim that he is not a socialist.

"If it looks like a duck and walks like a duck and quacks like a duck, it's a duck," House GOP Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain, R-Mich., told Fox News Digital. "So maybe he's not a socialist. Maybe he's a full-blown communist."

El-Sayed, a former public health official, scored an upset victory for Democrats' leftmost flank in Michigan's Senate primary earlier this month. He defeated Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., a House lawmaker who was heavily favored by the Democratic establishment, including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y.

It was part of a larger wave of victories by candidates aligned with the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), several of whom have toppled sitting House Democratic lawmakers in primaries in New York and Colorado in addition to Michigan.

2026 MIDTERMS STATE OF PLAY: KEY RACES UNFOLD AS STEVENS, EL-SAYED BATTLE IN MICHIGAN

And while El-Sayed himself is not a DSA member, some of the biggest names to campaign alongside him — including Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., and Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich. — are self-proclaimed democratic socialists.

El-Sayed told CBS News in an interview posted to YouTube last week that he was working on building a broad coalition that included supporters of President Donald Trump as well as DSA members, even though he is neither.

"Folks who come here, like, with two weeks left in the election, really, really want to label me a socialist. I don't know why, except for maybe it fits into a nice telling of a broader national story. But I'm a scientist, right? And I like solutions that solve problems," El-Sayed said. "I don't do ideology. I'd rather think of myself as a capitalist who actually read about capitalism, in the sense that the biggest risk to capitalism was always going to be corporate consolidation and monopoly, rather than government regulation."

McClain, meanwhile, argued that El-Sayed's platform is inherently socialist.

"He wants to take money out of your pockets. He wants free everything. Well, at the end of the day, if everything is free, someone has to pay for it," McClain said. "Are the farmers not gonna get paid? Are the teachers not going to get paid? He wants higher taxes, and he wants to take money out of your pockets so you can pay for your neighbors. To me, that's socialism. That's borderline communism."

MICHIGAN SENATE CANDIDATE ABDUL EL-SAYED DODGES QUESTION ON WHETHER HE STILL SUPPORTS DEFUNDING THE POLICE

El-Sayed's policy platform includes promises to fight for Medicare for all, raising taxes on millionaires and billionaires, using "wage insurance and basic income" programs to counter artificial intelligence automating industries, and abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), according to his website.

Republicans have argued that the majority of policies supported by the progressive and socialist left will amount to higher taxes for everyday Americans. But Democrats have insisted that their plans will lead to more affordable living for working- and middle-class people.

Traditionally, the party in power in the White House tends to lose seats in Congress during the midterms. That, combined with low approval numbers for President Donald Trump, means Republicans have an uphill battle to buck past political trends to keep control of the House and Senate.

But McClain pointed out that El-Sayed failed to clinch an outright majority in Michigan Democrats' Senate primary and predicted it would mean Republicans running up and down the ballot in the Wolverine State will see big gains with the far-left progressive at the top of the ticket.

BIDEN-WORLD VETERAN ISSUES STARK WARNING ABOUT ABDUL EL-SAYED AS HE CROSSES PARTY LINES

"I think it's gonna help us tremendously, right? Because if you look at El-Sayed's numbers, 50%, over 50% — the majority didn't vote for him. So what are those voters gonna do?" McClain posed. "How is El-Sayed and his crazy progressive, socialist, communist party going to bring those Democratic voters over to the Democratic side of the ticket? I don't think they are. MOSCOW, KYIV ASSASSINS HUNT WEAPONS BOSSES AS UKRAINE WAR SPILLS BEYOND THE BATTLEFIELD

Tusk also said Thursday that it was the first time that "someone on the order of Russia" sought to attack an American citizen on the territory of another NATO country, The Associated Press reported.

The operation was carried out in cooperation with U.S. services, Tomasz Siemoniak, Poland’s minister overseeing intelligence services, told the AP.

The news agency reported that it has mapped about 200 acts of sabotage, arson and other disruption across Europe since the start of the Ukraine war that officials have linked to Russia. President Vladimir Putin claimed to the AP in May that Russia is not waging a sabotage campaign against Europe.

RUSSIA LINKED TO ARSON ATTACKS ON PROPERTIES CONNECTED TO UK PM KEIR STARMER, POLICE SAY

Last year, French officials disrupted a plot which they believe was aimed at killing Vladimir Osechkin, a Russian exile who lives under police protection and works to help military defectors flee Putin’s war.

Lithuanian officials also disrupted a plot last year to kill a Lithuanian supporter of Ukraine and another against a Russian activist.

Officials in Germany have similarly broken up two plots: one to target the head of a German weapons company supplying Ukraine, the other against a Ukrainian military official.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: How a noncitizen suspected killer got caught and released by Newsom-appointed judge: timeline
item.description: Surveillance video allegedly shows Marcos Iriarte-Valdez in a tactical vest stabbing retiree Todd Stewart in a quiet East Bay suburb of California.
item.content:encoded:
The suspect charged in the stabbing death of a California man in an otherwise quiet East Bay suburb has a history of prior arrests and originally entered the U.S. during the George W. Bush administration, according to records.

Marcos Iriarte-Valdez, alternatively identified by DHS as Marcos Valdezusper, was arrested Friday at his home in Contra Costa County, California, after police said he stabbed and killed 68-year-old retiree Todd Stewart during an apparent burglary attempt.

"The investigation is ongoing and our understanding of the incident may change as more individuals are interviewed and evidence is collected and analyzed," the Martinez Police Department said.

Iriarte-Valdez was "legally admitted" to the U.S. in 2007, according to information provided by ICE. Fox News Digital reached out to the agency for further clarity on what happened between then and when he was deemed an "illegal alien" by DHS on X more recently.

DEADLY HOSPITAL STABBING PUTS NEWSOM UNDER PRESSURE OVER ICE DETAINER FIGHT

Iriarte-Valdez hails from Venezuela but has Spanish citizenship.

Iriarte-Valdez was arrested earlier this year on at least two charges of residential burglary with persons present stemming from incidents in Orinda April 29, according to Martinez police.

He was out on pretrial release for those charges when he was arrested again Aug. 4 for violating his home detention monitoring rules, according to authorities.

FEDS ADMIT FAILURE TO DISCLOSE MURDER WARRANT TO JUDGE WHO ORDERED RELEASE OF DOMINICAN MIGRANT

One day later, Contra Costa Superior Court Judge Nichelle Holmes, an appointee of Gov. Gavin Newsom, released Iriarte-Valdez on his own recognizance and returned him to home detention monitoring.

Then, on Aug. 6, surveillance video showed Iriarte-Valdez wearing a tactical vest and emerging from a Cadillac before he allegedly stabbed Stewart, who was heard screaming in pain.

That video helped police obtain a warrant from Contra Costa Superior Court for Iriarte-Valdez on charges of murder and committing a felony while on own-recognizance release, according to court records.

Just after 6 p.m. PT Friday, a Contra Costa SWAT team arrested Iriarte-Valdez at his home. His bail was initially set at $1.1 million.

ICE LODGES DETAINER FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ACCUSED OF TRYING TO DISARM VIRGINIA POLICE OFFICER

Contra Costa County Democratic District Attorney Diane Becton filed a felony complaint against Iriarte-Valdez that included one count of murder with several "special circumstances" cited under California law that could result in stiffer penalties.

The complaint includes a special circumstance allegation of murder during a burglary, which could lead to life imprisonment without parole if Iriarte-Valdez is convicted and "enhancement" allegations involving the use of a knife and committing an offense while out on conditional release.

"Our office will pursue this case with diligence and integrity to hold Iriarte-Valdez fully accountable under the law for this devastating act of violence," Becton said in a statement.

"Our thoughts are with the victim’s loved ones and the larger community as they navigate this unimaginable loss."

MAN CHARGED IN CRASH THAT KILLED MOTHER AND TWO YOUNG SONS HAS ICE DETAINER, PRIOR DWI CONVICTIONS

Becton’s office said Iriarte-Valdez pleaded not guilty Wednesday during a hearing in which Judge David Goldstein called him a "risk to public safety" and ordered him held without bail. Former Democratic Gov. Jerry Brown appointed Goldstein.

Another Newsom appointee, Judge Michael Nieto, will preside over Iriarte-Valdez’s case during a preliminary hearing in nearby Richmond Sept. 1.

According to court documents, Iriarte-Valdez is scheduled to appear separately before Holmes on Sept. 9 on his original burglary charges from April.

ICE placed a federal detainer on Iriarte-Valdez Saturday and said he has also been charged with inflicting corporal injury on a spouse, receiving stolen property, trespassing, loitering and entering a noncommercial dwelling.

TOM HOMAN WARNS ICE SURGE COMING TO NEW YORK CITY AS MAMDANI BOASTS ABOUT SANCTUARY STATUS

DHS did not immediately explain what happened between 2007 and 2026 that could have led to Iriarte-Valdez being considered an "illegal alien" now. Common scenarios include a noncitizen overstaying a temporary visa, violating visa terms, becoming a lawful permanent resident and later having that status revoked because of a criminal conviction or abandoning permanent resident status through extended residency abroad.

White House border czar Thomas Homan described the incident as a tragic case of "politics of a sanctuary jurisdiction."

"There's nothing against the sanctuary law in California for a deputy to pick a phone up and say, 'Hey, this guy's being let go in an hour,'" Homan told "Fox & Friends." 

"This person is dead because Governor Newsom and the State of California put politics — hatred of President Trump — over public safety."

Fox News Digital reached out to Holmes, Becton and Newsom for further comment.

item.title: Haley Stevens condemns Hasan Piker but rallies behind El-Sayed after narrow primary loss
